title: Optimizing 4D STEM Data Collection and Processing for Crystal Orientation Mapping Analysis in DigitalMicrograph
content: Crystal orientation mapping using 4D STEM is a desirable technique because it enables higher resolution analysis of nanograined materials that are difficult to study via EBSD in the SEM. 4D STEM experiments also frequently make sure of high speed and high sensitivity on-axis cameras to acquire diffraction patterns with high dynamic range and good signal to noise ratios (SNR). To date, the most accessible way of calculating orientation maps from 4D STEM data is by using open-source programs like py4DSTEM [1] or pyxem [2], but these solutions require users to be familiar with Python scripting to generate results. This abstract introduces the new STEMx® OIM software from Gatan. STEMx OIM enables orientation mapping analysis of 4D STEM data directly inside of DigitalMicrograph® and without the need for scripting. Therefore, users can calculate orientation maps while utilizing the full potential of Gatan high-speed and high-sensitivity cameras, in addition to energy-filtering and multimodal data collection (e.g., 4D STEM + EDS) with eaSI™ technology. Exploring the full parameter space of the hardware and software toolkit from Gatan results in high-quality 4D STEM data with excellent orientation mapping results from STEMx OIM.
